answers.question: I feel ready. Can I go back to 40 miles next week and start speedwork for the 10K?
answers.answer:
Short answer: not yet on either one. You followed the recovery week well and the legs clearly feel good, but a jump from 12 to 40 miles in a single step, with speedwork on top, is the classic way to turn a happy post-marathon body into a hurt one. The deep tissue repair from a 3:50 marathon runs well past the point where the legs feel normal.

Here is what I would like to do instead. This week we go to roughly 24 miles across five days, all easy, with a few short strides mid-week to wake the legs up without stressing them. Next week we can step toward 32 or so, and the week after that, if everything still feels good, we open the door to one real session, likely a short tempo or 10K-pace cruise intervals.

On the Thanksgiving 10K: it is five weeks out, which is enough time to sharpen if you want it, but I would treat it as a tune-up effort rather than a peak race. Confirm you want to run it and I will build the next three weeks around it.

new.analysis:
## Where you are

You are two weeks out from a 3:50 marathon, a 12-minute lifetime best, and the recovery week went exactly as planned: three easy runs, 12 miles, heart rate drifting back down and effort scores low. That is the picture of a body doing its job.

## Why I am holding the reins

The reason to go slow now is not how you feel, it is what you did. A 3h 50m race at zone 4 for most of it leaves micro-damage that outlasts the soreness by a couple of weeks. The research-backed rule of thumb is one easy day per mile raced, which is a lot, and I am already compressing that because you are clearly fine. Giving back the fitness you built is very hard; getting hurt chasing a tune-up 10K is easy.

## What this week does

We add the fifth running day back, nudge the long run to 8 miles, and sprinkle a handful of 20-second strides into Wednesday so the legs remember what turnover feels like. No tempo, no intervals, nothing in zone 3 or above on purpose. If anything feels off, cut it short, that is still a win this week.

## What I need from you

Tell me whether the Thanksgiving 10K is a go, and whether you want a next marathon on the calendar. The shape of November and December depends entirely on that answer, and I would rather plan around a real target than guess.
